title: feat(cli): os serve publishes its datasource secret store's resolve as the datasource-secret-resolver service, so a stack's OData plugin resolves a sys_secret credentialsRef with no code
body:
epic:#27261#1 · marchtian · session_017ihL2fy9PSGEZJdJpoPvzx
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"marchtian"} -->
_Requested by **田騏** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi?thread=cmsg_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi7GiMpxi6VR7nKYEhHVxChB)_

**Fable review owed.** Developed on Opus while the Fable quota is out. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (a new published kernel service), so it lands after a contract review PASS on the current head.

Fixes #27875

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** `os serve` 把它为数据源建的密钥解析器的「读」那一半（`resolve`）注册成内核服务 `datasource-secret-resolver`。OData 插件没拿到 `options.secrets` 时，在第一个请求时去读这个服务，于是 `credentialsRef: 'sys_secret:…'` 在 `os serve` 上不用写代码就能解析。显式传的 `options.secrets` 仍然优先；两者都没有时照旧拒绝请求，什么都不发出去，报错里点名这个服务。
- **为什么改：** 声明式 OData 的卖点是只写元数据。凭据这一步要作者自己写 `resolve`，卖点就破了（#27871 写指南时发现）。
- **风险与回滚：** 只发布 `resolve`，`bind`/`unbind` 仍只在数据源管理插件手里；它只解得开 `datasource_credential` 作用域封的行，设置项密钥和密钥字段的行解不开（有测试）。没有加密提供者时 `os serve` 不建解析器，也就不注册服务。进程内任何插件都能调这个 `resolve`；为什么可以接受（信任边界是进程，引擎的 `resolveSecret` 已对进程内调用方解密密钥字段），见 What changes 一节。回滚即 revert。
- **文档：** OData 指南（`odata-datasources.mdx`，#27871 已落地）去掉了「`os serve` 下要自己传 `resolve`」的说明，改为：`os serve` 下不传 `secrets`，凭据走服务端自己的密钥存储。
- **先看：** `packages/types/src/datasource-secret-resolver.ts`（服务名、接口、插件驱动该怎么读）；`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` 的 `createDatasourceSecretResolverPlugin` 和挂载处；`packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/plugin.ts` 的 `hostSecretResolver`。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run src/commands/serve-datasource-secret-resolver.test.ts`，预期 5 个用例全绿：真内核加真 binder，绑定的凭据经服务解出原文，服务上只有 `resolve`，别的生产者封的行解不开。
- **需要您做的：** 无。契约复审 PASS 后落地。

## What changes

**The service and its contract** (`packages/types/src/datasource-secret-resolver.ts`): `DATASOURCE_SECRET_RESOLVER_SERVICE` (`'datasource-secret-resolver'`) and `IDatasourceSecretResolver` (`resolve(credentialsRef)`, answering `undefined` for a handle that is not the binder's, a missing row or a decrypt failure). The module states how every plugin driver that dereferences an `external.credentialsRef` reads it: an explicit secret store handed to the plugin first; the service looked up at the first request, never at `init()` (AGENTS.md, "Startup registry reads"); fail-closed when neither resolves. It lives in `@objectstack/types` because the producer (`os serve`) and the consumers (plugin drivers, in this repository or out of it) never import each other, and the package depends only on `@objectstack/spec`. The card asked whether other plugin drivers should read it the same way: yes, and the module is where that is written down.

**The producer** (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`): `createDatasourceSecretResolverPlugin(secrets)` (plugin `com.objectstack.cli.datasource-secret-resolver`, `providesServices: ['datasource-secret-resolver']`) registers a resolver whose one method calls the binder's `resolve`. `run()` mounts it right after `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin`, with the same binder, and only when a binder was built. No crypto provider means no binder, so no service, and a driver's refusal names the service.

**The consumer** (`packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/plugin.ts`, the `secrets` fallback only): `const store = secrets ?? hostSecretResolver(ctxRef)`, evaluated inside the per-request `credential()` provider. `hostSecretResolver` catches the kernel's throw on an unregistered name, so the miss reaches the plugin's own refusal, not the kernel's "not found" text. The refusal message gains the service name and the two remedies (run under `os serve`, or pass `options.secrets`). It reads the service through `@objectstack/types`, which the package already depends on since #27819.

**The guide** (`content/docs/data-modeling/odata-datasources.mdx`, landed with #27871 while this was in progress): the mount example drops its `secrets: erpSecretStore` line and import; the option table says an absent `secrets` falls back to the host's `datasource-secret-resolver` service, which `os serve` registers; the Credentials section replaces the "pass your own resolve on os serve" caveat with the two cases (under `os serve`, pass nothing; a host composing its own kernel passes `secrets` or registers the service) and the fail-closed list says "neither `secrets` nor the service".

**Who can call `resolve`, and why that is acceptable.** Any plugin in the process can read the service and call `resolve()` on any `sys_secret:` handle. It is not narrowed to the calling datasource's own `credentialsRef`, because the service cannot tell who calls it, and the measured alternatives narrow nothing real:

- **The trust boundary is the process, not the plugin.** A plugin is code the operator installed and runs with the kernel's own reach: it can read `sys_secret` rows under the system context through the data engine, and the engine's public `resolveSecret` already decrypts a secret field's `secret:` reference for any in-process caller (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `resolveSecret`). This service adds no reach of a new kind; it adds the datasource credentials, through the binder the datasource admin already holds.
- **What it can open is bounded by scope.** The binder decrypts under the `datasource_credential` crypto scope alone, so a settings secret or a secret field's row fails authentication and answers `undefined` (pinned in the new cli test). `bind` and `unbind` are not on the service.
- **"Only a handle some declared datasource names" would not narrow it.** Every datasource definition, with its `credentialsRef`, is readable by any plugin through the engine's `listDatasourceDefs()`, so such a check excludes only orphaned handles while adding a second read on every request. A per-caller restriction needs a caller identity the kernel's service registry does not carry.
- **The alternative a stricter host has** is to not publish it: `os serve` mounts it only when it mounts the datasource admin itself, and a host composing its own kernel registers the service or passes `secrets` explicitly.

**Ledger:** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the new test's `sys_secret` double (its `delete` routes through `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`), written by `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write` as the gate asks.

**Changeset:** `patch` on `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/driver-odata` (`Metadata-protocol: none` takes patch).

## Why

Epic #27261 P2 (ruling 6486145005, Tier B = declarative OData). Found by #27747's carrier (#27871, os-dev-report 6513440511): on `origin/main`, `serve.ts` builds `createDatasourceSecretBinder` and hands it only to `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin`, so a stack's OData plugin cannot resolve a `sys_secret:` handle under `os serve`.

## Verification

On `cf00041b` (`origin/main` merged in three times, last after #27819 landed at `ed8b2375`; #27871 and the driver-odata conformance kit came in the merge before), after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and a full build of `./packages/**` (exit 0):

- **New tests.** `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-datasource-secret-resolver.test.ts` (5): inside a real `ObjectKernel` over a real binder (`createDatasourceSecretBinder` with `LocalCryptoProvider`), a credential bound through the binder resolves through the service to its cleartext; the service's only key is `resolve`; a settings-scoped row in the same `sys_secret` table, a missing row and a foreign handle all answer `undefined`; `providesServices` names the service; and a source pin (comments masked) that `run()` mounts the plugin inside `if (secrets)` with that binder and defines it once. `packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/plugin.test.ts` (5 new): the handle resolves through the host's service with no `options.secrets` and the service is asked exactly once; an explicit `options.secrets` wins and the service is never asked; a handle the service does not resolve is refused with nothing sent; a service registered after the plugin's `init` is seen at the first request; and on a real kernel with neither, the refusal is the plugin's own message naming the service, never the kernel's text, with nothing sent. The existing "no secret store" refusal row is unchanged.
- **Ablations, each red then restored** (`git status --porcelain` empty after each): the fallback removed (`const store = secrets`): 3 failed; precedence flipped (service before `options.secrets`): 1 failed; the `getService` try/catch removed: 1 failed (the real-kernel case); the whole binder registered instead of the read half: 1 failed.
- **Suites:** `driver-odata` 732 passed (the connector-credential cases included); `types` 832 passed; `cli` the two `serve-datasource-*` files, 11 passed. `typecheck` exit 0 for `types`, `driver-odata` and `cli` (the cli run includes `check:test-typecheck`).
- **Local gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 101 families from the changed files on that head; every one was run with its exit code recorded before any pipe, and `dispatch-gates --ran` reads "101 derived, 101 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)" (112 of 112 on the pre-#27819 head `33bc41fb`). PR CI on `cf00041b`: every required check `success`. An earlier pass on the pre-guide head was red on three gates about the new test's double, all fixed in the diff: `check:engine-double-contract` (the double's `delete` now routes through `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`, ledger row written), `check:where-matcher` (the operator refusal moved inside the matcher callback) and `check:cross-package-test-inputs` (a doc comment named another package's test path). The full battery (`pnpm lint`, Test Core shards, UI jobs) is CI's. No dogfood run: no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm.

## Acceptance notes

- **#27819 (#27746) landed first** (`ed8b2375`), so this PR merged `main` and resolved the one conflict in `plugin.ts`: the header keeps both sections (the `credentialsRef` channel with its service fallback, and the borrowed connector credential), one `@objectstack/types` import carries both service names, and `credential()` keeps `secrets ?? hostSecretResolver(ctxRef)` beside `borrowed()`. In `plugin.test.ts` the new cases take `main`'s `boot(options, defs, { services })` signature. The `@objectstack/types` dependency and its lockfile lines are now `main`'s, so neither is in this diff.
- **The README** (`packages/drivers/driver-odata/README.md`, added at the epic PM's request): the mount example no longer passes `secrets` and says the handle resolves through the host's service, and the Config table gains the `secrets` row. This edit rides in the merge commit `cf00041b`.
- **One file outside the claim's list:** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (the ledger row the gate requires for the new test double; it only grows coverage).
- **How this meets #27819 (#27746).** #27819 reshapes `plugin.ts` around a `definition()` helper and a `borrowed()` connector path; this PR edits only the `if (!secrets)` block inside `credential()` plus one helper and one import, so the two should meet as a small textual conflict in `credential()`. Whichever lands second takes the other's lines; the package.json and lockfile lines for `@objectstack/types` are identical in both. The `types/src/index.ts` export sits away from #27819's hunk.
- **A stack that registers its own `datasource-secret-resolver`** collides with `os serve`'s at boot (`Service 'datasource-secret-resolver' already registered`), loudly. `os serve` mounts its plugin only when it mounts the datasource admin itself, so a stack that brings its own admin plugin gets no second one.
- **Worktree name:** the claim names `objectstack-issue-27875`; the worktree is `objectstack-27875` on the claimed branch.
